task_summary: Unified react-pdf-highlighter-plus PDF annotation workspace replacing legacy viewer with multi-layer annotation adapter: 1) Viewport-independent ScaledPosition adapter bridging MongoDB comment.model.js ({x,y,width,height,pageNumber}) and plagiarism report spans. 2) Core PdfViewerWorkspace with custom highlight renderer, popup popover, threaded replies, and Flag to ADM integration. 3) Dual-pipeline plagiarism overlay using PDF.js text layer scan (getTextPosition) and diagonal striped cross-layer overlap detection (.archive-mark-overlap). 4) Split-screen EvaluationWorkspace (55% PDF / 45% tabbed drawer for Rubrics, ADM, and Sources) with sticky defense verdict bar, layer filtering ([All], [Comments], [Plagiarism]), and 100% semantic design tokens (bg-background, text-foreground, border-border, bg-card, bg-muted). 5) Embedded in canonical SophisticatedDocumentViewer with useLegacyIframe fallback. Passed 21/21 client unit tests across 4 test suites, 207/188 endpoint parity (UNMATCHED_COUNT=0), 60/60 agentic validation checks, pristine workspace guardrails, and 9-point Playwright visual audit across desktop and mobile viewports in light and dark themes.

lessons_learned.context: react-pdf-highlighter-plus PdfLoader workerSrc defaults to relative URL against ESM dist package which returns 404 in Vite development servers. Always explicitly provide document={pdfUrl} and workerSrc='/pdf.worker.min.mjs' props.
Ensure public/pdf.worker.min.mjs is maintained in client/public and synchronized with pdfjs-dist version in client/package.json.

When adding or refactoring evaluation workspaces, use CSS semantic design system tokens (bg-background, text-foreground, bg-card, bg-muted, border-border) instead of literal slate classes to preserve WCAG AAA contrast in both Light and Dark modes.
